articles.mainContent:
Choosing a full-time caregiver is a big decision. Nannies may spend tons of time with your kids, shaping their days and influencing their growth. That's why you need someone you can trust.

As a recruitment specialist with extensive experience in background checks, I've helped many families navigate this process. The key is thorough vetting that goes beyond basic qualifications. You'll also want to verify skills like first aid and CPR and get real insights from previous employers.

To make your search easier, I've created a five-step guide. It will help you assess candidates carefully and choose a nanny who's truly right for your family. Let's dive in.

» Find out why you should run a background check before hiring a nanny.

1. Contact Previous Employers for References

A resume can be deceiving. In fact, 64.2% of employees have lied about skills, experience, or references at least once. Spend some time contacting references and asking about a candidate's work history.

When talking to previous employers, focus on the potential nanny's on-the-job performance, skills, and temperament. Don't shy away from asking about conflicts or negative experiences. To make these conversations easier, try these questions:

About the Job

  • What was the caregiver's role?
  • How long did they work for you?

Personality

  • How would you describe the caregiver?
  • What did you like most about them?
  • Was there anything you disliked?
  • Did your children enjoy their time with the caregiver?

Professionalism

  • Were they always on time for work?
  • How did they handle emergencies?
  • Did they perform their duties to your liking?
  • Did they ever drive your children around?
  • Do they need a lot of guidance and supervision?
  • What areas could they improve?
  • Why did they leave?
  • Would you hire them again?

2. Check Criminal History and Other Violations

A criminal history check can help you weed out nannies unsuitable for caring for your kids. These checks can help you identify a history of child abuse, violence, or anger issues. It's also the perfect time to look out for DUIs or drug abuse violations.

Just remember to do everything by the book. Ensure you know how to conduct a criminal background check and follow state and federal guidelines.

3. Verify Your Nanny's Qualifications

When hiring a nanny, focus on these essential education verification tips:

  • Education: Start with a high school diploma as the baseline. An Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Early Childhood Education is even better, indicating a solid grasp of child development.
  • Certifications: Look for relevant childcare credentials. Advanced certifications like Certified Nanny and Childcare Provider (NCP) or Certified Newborn and Infant Care Professional (NICP) are particularly valuable.
  • Safety skills: Prioritize candidates with current Pediatric First Aid and CPR certifications. Swimming ability is crucial if you have a pool. Don't overlook the importance of a valid driver's license for handling emergencies.

Review these qualifications on resumes and discuss them during interviews. Always verify credentials using trusted background check services like CheckPeople or TruthFinder. This approach ensures you select a nanny with the right skills and background to provide safe, quality care for your children.

Remember, supporting your nanny's continued professional growth benefits your entire family. Encourage their participation in workshops and pursuit of new certifications to ensure they stay current with childcare best practices.

» Don't miss a thing. Learn about the best practices for background checks.

4. Evaluate Their Personal Background

Video Interviews

Consider conducting initial video interviews before in-person meetings. This approach allows you to screen candidates and observe their communication skills. Pay attention to their demeanor, clarity of speech, and how they present themselves in a virtual setting.

In-person Interview

Resumes and background checks only tell part of the story. The real purpose of your interview is to gauge the candidate's maturity, reliability, and ability to handle responsibilities. Use this time to dig deeper into their character and approach to childcare.

Discuss Childcare Approach

Start by asking about their approach to childcare and related challenges. Inquire about their parenting philosophy, how they manage difficult children, and the safety measures they take when out with kids. These questions will give you a clearer picture of how they'll care for your children.

Explore Personal Interests

Next, delve into their personal hobbies, activities, and interests that might affect the job. Ask if there are sports or activities they'd like to share with the children. It's also wise to inquire about any extra-curricular activities or responsibilities that could impact their availability.

Social Media Screening

Social media background checks reveal a lot about potential employees. Reviewing a candidate's online presence will give you insights into their personality, interests, and communication style. You might see how they interact with children or handle childcare situations.

Before checking social media, always get the candidate's written permission. Focus on public, professional information rather than personal details. Use a service like BeenVerified if you want help conducting these checks properly.

5. Comply with Legal Requirements

Follow Proper Procedures

The Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) governs background checks. You must get permission before accessing consumer reports with criminal history information. Be aware of this law to protect yourself and the candidate.

Follow adverse action procedures if you decide not to hire someone. Give them a written explanation for your decision. This step protects you from legal issues and prevents discrimination based on race, gender, or sexual orientation.

Know Your State and Local Laws

Check your area's background check rules before hiring a nanny. Laws vary widely by location. For example, in California, you can't consider arrests that didn't lead to convictions or convictions older than seven years.

When reviewing a candidate's record, you should:

  • Balance past offenses with their efforts to improve
  • Consider only what's legally allowed in your area
  • Be aware of fair chance laws like "ban the box," which may delay when you can ask about criminal history
  • Stick to relevant, public information and avoid using private records

These steps help you make fair decisions and stay within the law. If you're unsure, consult a local employment lawyer for guidance, or consider platforms like Intelius and Instant Checkmate.

» Discover these tips for choosing the best background check site.

Implement a Trial Period

Before making a final hiring decision, consider implementing a paid trial period or "working interview." This approach lets you observe the nanny's interactions with your kids in a real-world setting. During this time, assess how well they handle your family's routines and any unexpected situations.

Use this period to ensure there's mutual compatibility between the nanny, your children, and your family as a whole. A trial period can reveal aspects of a nanny's working style and personality that might not be apparent in traditional interviews or background checks.

Plan for Ongoing Monitoring

Hiring a nanny is not a one-time event but an ongoing process. Plan to conduct periodic background checks (with the nanny's consent) to stay informed of any changes in their record. Schedule regular performance reviews to discuss any concerns, provide feedback, and set goals.

Stay alert to any changes in behavior or circumstances that might affect their work. If you choose to use nanny cams, ensure you're aware of and compliant with local laws regarding surveillance. Ongoing monitoring helps maintain a safe environment for your children and a professional relationship with your nanny.

Conduct Nanny Background Checks Responsibly

When screening potential nannies, handle all information with care and discretion. Keep the intel confidential, and don't share it without the candidate's consent. During interviews, be professional and transparent. This responsible approach helps protect everyone's privacy, avoid legal issues, and maintain trust.

Use a service like PeopleLooker as a tool to make informed decisions, not as a way to gather unnecessary personal information. By following these guidelines, you can conduct thorough screenings while respecting candidates' rights and maintaining ethical hiring practices.

When screening potential employees, small business owners must navigate legal requirements carefully. Here's what you need to know:

  • Consent requirements: Always ask candidates for permission before running a background check. This protects your business legally and maintains transparency.
  • Protect personal data: To protect candidate data, use strong passwords and encryption, limit access to necessary staff, securely store and dispose of information, and train employees on properly handling sensitive data.
  • Know your local laws: Many areas have "fair chance" or "ban-the-box" laws. These rules may limit when you can ask about criminal history, giving candidates a fair shot at employment.
  • Avoid discrimination: The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) prohibits hiring decisions based on race, religion, gender, or national origin. Evaluate all candidates fairly.
  • Stay informed: Keep up with changing state and federal laws regarding background checks in your area.

Types of Background Checks

Using different types of background checks can help you understand the candidate holistically. Consider combining and incorporating the following types of checks in your process:

Criminal History Checks

When running a criminal background check, choose a trusted screening service that follows legal guidelines. Small businesses can try an affordable option like Answer Lady. Look at convictions, not arrests, and think about how serious the offense is and if it matters for the job.

For instance, a drunk driving conviction might not be a big deal for an accountant working in an office, but it would be for someone who drives for work.

Employment Verification

Go beyond simply confirming job titles and dates. Contact previous employers for insights into the candidate's work ethic, team dynamics, and ability to handle specific challenges relevant to your business.

For example, if you're a marketing agency, ask about the candidate's experience managing client relationships or meeting tight deadlines. This process can uncover valuable information not apparent on a resume.

Education Verification

When checking education credentials, contact schools directly or use a service like BeenVerfied. This is crucial for roles needing specific qualifications, like IT or healthcare positions. Be aware that some candidates might exaggerate their experience.

Smart interviewers use education verification tips beyond just checking paperwork. During interviews, casually ask candidates how they've applied their degree in previous jobs or discuss relevant coursework. This can help you verify their claims while assessing their practical knowledge.

Professional License Verification

For jobs needing special licenses, like nurses or electricians, ensure the candidate's credentials are valid and up-to-date. Check with the relevant licensing board to see if there's any history of problems. This protects your business and keeps you in line with industry rules.

Motor Vehicle Record Checks

If you're hiring someone who'll drive for work, like a delivery person or sales rep, check their driving record. Look for recent tickets or accidents that might raise red flags on background checks.

A clean record usually means a responsible driver, which is safer for your business. Consider how serious any violations are—a speeding ticket from five years ago might not be as concerning as a recent reckless driving charge.

Challenges of Performing Background Checks

Cost Constraints

The cost of background checks is a major factor for small businesses. Professional checks can range from $18 to $35 per candidate, straining tight budgets, especially when hiring multiple positions.

US Search is ideal for small businesses looking for a cost-effective solution. Its plans start at just $14.95/month and include reverse phone and email lookups. The platform can give you all the data you need to qualify and understand potential hires without breaking the bank.

Screening Delays

You might lose great candidates during lengthy background checks. These screenings often take weeks, giving your competitors a chance to snatch up talent. That's why you should be up-front about any pre-employment screening delays.

Your transparency and communication will help keep top candidates interested, even if the background check takes longer than ideal. However, if you're in a rush to fill a position quickly, InstantCheckmate can provide a quick turnaround of 12 minutes.

Legal Compliance

Legal compliance in background checks can challenge small businesses without dedicated HR departments. Smaller teams often struggle to keep up with evolving federal, state, and local regulations. However, failing to comply can expose your business to costly lawsuits or fines.

To protect your business, consider consulting with an employment lawyer or using a reputable background check service like PeopleFinder that stays current on regulations.

Small Business Hiring With Peace of Mind

For small businesses, background checks are more than just a hiring formality—they're a vital tool for protecting and growing your company. While the process may require some investment of time and resources, it's far less costly than the potential risks of a bad hire.

By carefully vetting candidates, you'll build a foundation of trust and competence to support your business as it grows.

articles.subtitle: If you date online, it's essential that you know how to protect your privacy and money from catfishers.
articles.summary: If you date online, it's essential that you know how to protect your privacy and money from catfishers.
articles.mainContent:
Many people worry about fake profiles when dating online. Some are new, but many catfishers have been doing this for a while and are good at hiding who they really are. Falling for these fake profiles can waste your time, trick you out of your money, or even make you give up on dating.

As a dating coach, I always tell my clients to verify profiles and confirm the true identities of their potential matches. Background checks are a surefire way to get confirmation and peace of mind, but there are additional safety precautions you can take, too. Here are 10 practical strategies to help protect yourself when dating online.

» Want a professional screening? Check out our top picks for the best background check sites for dating.

1. Confirm Their Account Is Verified

Online dating sites sometimes ask users to take a selfie resembling their profile picture. This helps prove they are who they say they are. After doing this, they get a badge on their profile showing others their identity is verified.

So, stay alert and only chat with people with a verified checkmark on their profile.

2. Check Their Social Media

Many dating apps let you link your social media, like Instagram, to your profile. This means others can see your social media photos right from the app. Some apps even require you to link a social media account to sign up.

But be careful! If someone is faking their identity, they might make a new social media profile to trick people. If you see a brand-new account, it could be a sign of something "fishy." So, always check how old someone's social media account is when you can.

» Scrolling through their feed? Use social media to help with a background check.

3. Use Trusted Apps or Dating Sites

Some dating apps use a friend-invite system to prevent impersonation. This helps keep the app's community exclusive and makes sure people are who they say they are.

But plenty of trusted apps and services are equipped with teams to eliminate fake profiles from the user experience. For example, eharmony has a trusted ID verification system, which aims to weed out catfishers, but if you're unsure, a background check can provide peace of mind.

4. Perform a Background Check

While not all dating platforms perform background checks, many require ID verification to enhance user safety. However, this typically does not include a criminal background check.

For a more thorough online dating check, I'd use a tool like TruthFinder. This service offers unlimited access to name, phone number, and address lookups. It also explores the deep web—the part of the internet not readily accessible by standard search engines. This means you can get a comprehensive view of someone’s online activity, including information they might prefer to keep hidden.

» Don't know what to look for on a report? Here are 10 red flags on a background check

5. Verify Their Phone Number

Dating apps usually ask for your phone number when you sign up. They send a code to your phone to make sure it's really you. But remember, this doesn't mean you're safe. Consider using online tools that let you search who a phone number belongs to, like reverse phone lookup services.

By typing in a phone number, you can find the name of the person who owns it, where the number has been used, and any social media profiles linked to it. Background check services like BeenVerified provide extensive reports on a given phone number, offering another layer of security in your online dating experience.

6. Use Video Chat for Identity Verification

Video chat features on dating platforms provide a straightforward way to confirm someone’s identity. If someone avoids video calls or hanging out, they might hide something about who they are.

So, if you’re comfortable, request a video chat—it’s my preferred way to simply and effectively verify someone’s identity.

7. Scrutinize Their Photos

Photos can reveal a lot about a person’s authenticity on online dating platforms. The account might be fake or misleading if there are only a few or really old photos.

Use a tool like Google's reverse image search to check if a photo is real. This lets you see where else the picture appears online. Just upload the photo, and Google will show you similar images. If the same photo is on someone else's profile, the person might be pretending to be someone they're not.

8. Look for Inconsistencies In Information

Check if what they say in their messages matches their profile. If they give conflicting information about things like their age, where they live, their job, or hobbies, that's suspicious. Remember the things they tell you over time. They might be lying if their stories change or don't add up.

I observe their communication patterns closely. If there are significant variations in their texting style, it could indicate they're copying from another source. The timing of their responses, especially if unusually quick or at odd hours, might suggest they're not genuinely who they claim to be. Additionally, regular significant updates to their profile—such as job, location, or personal details—could be a sign of deceit.

9. Be Wary of Rapid Escalation of the Relationship

Catfishers often try to speed up the progression of your relationship, expressing strong feelings or suggesting serious commitment unusually early. This tactic, known as “love bombing,” is used to manipulate and control the pace and direction of your relationship.

Be careful if someone wants immediate commitment, isolation from others, and pushes you for personal info. Be extra wary if they say they're in love with you soon after you meet.

10. Turn Down Requests for Money or Financial Information

Romance scams are rife. Consumers lost around $547 million in 2021 to dating swindlers. If someone you've met online asks for your financial details, that's a big red flag. Never share details with someone you've met online, such as your bank account number, credit card information, or other sensitive data.

These requests can come in many forms. Some may directly ask for money, citing a sudden personal crisis or a desire to meet you in person. Others may be more subtle, asking for your financial information under the guise of sending you gifts or sharing investment opportunities.

Catfishing: The Truth Lies in the Details

I envision a future where online dating becomes more regulated, with legal consequences for misconduct. If online dating continues to be a popular way for people to meet and date, there needs to be more real-time monitoring to ensure user safety.

Until then, it’s important to closely examine a person’s photos and words. My clients tend to swipe through photos quickly and don’t take the time to scrutinize a profile. However, the devil is in the details, and inconsistencies are easier to catch when you slow down. So, take your time and stay vigilant.

Picking the wrong tenant can be more than just a nuisance; it can lead to significant financial strain. Surveys show the average US household spends around $1,570 a year on maintenance and repairs. Imagine how those numbers soar when you're dealing with property damage from careless tenants.

Thankfully, top background check services allow you to vet potential tenants before handing over the keys. By screening applicants thoroughly, you can minimize risks and protect your property investment. Let's explore 10 ways background checks help you avoid nightmare tenants.

» Need to vet potential tenants? Check out our landlord's guide to tenant screening.

1. Verifies Applicant Identity

Start your tenant screening process with identity verification. This crucial step ensures all subsequent checks are based on accurate information. It prevents applicants from hiding a problematic past under a false name, setting the foundation for an honest landlord-tenant relationship.

BeenVerified can assist in this process by cross-referencing provided information with public records and confirming the applicant's name, age, and address history. This thorough verification helps you confidently proceed with other screening steps, knowing you're dealing with the person they claim to be.

2. Uncovers Their Criminal History

Conducting a criminal background check isn't just a formality; it's a vital step in protecting your community. When you know that someone has a violent past, you're taking active measures to safeguard all your tenants.

Issues like substance abuse or vandalism can also pose serious risks to your property's security and overall harmony. A service like Intelius can help you uncover criminal records, providing valuable information to make informed decisions about potential tenants.

Remember that past mistakes don't always predict the future. It's crucial to balance safety and fairness, staying within legal limits to ensure everyone's rights are respected.

3. Reveals Credit History Issues

A thorough credit check can indicate how reliably a tenant will pay rent and manage their finances. Signs of bad credit might point to potential rent arrears or overall financial instability, which are red flags for any landlord.

Credit checks also reveal the tenant’s ability to cope with unexpected financial shocks, like layoffs. A good credit line suggests that they can still meet rent payments during tough times, ensuring a steady income flow for you despite unforeseen circumstances.

4. Checks Rental History

This check shows how long they've stayed at previous rentals and whether they've been consistent with their monthly payments. It's not just about duration and payments; it’s about commitment to rental agreements.

Rental history reports can also provide a glimpse into how tenants treat the properties they rent. Did they maintain the space well? Were there any complaints from previous landlords? These insights are invaluable in deciding whether they’ll be respectful and responsible tenants in your property.

5. Detects Eviction Records

Evictions are major red flags for any landlord, often leading to losses that can spiral into the thousands. TransUnion found that eviction-related expenses average around $3,500 for property managers, and the process can drag on for 3-4 weeks.

Examining a tenant's eviction history can help you spot recurring patterns that indicate problematic behavior. This could help you gauge their reliability and respect for rental agreements.

6. Verifies Employment Status

It's all about stability when you're renting out your property. Checking if a tenant has a steady job is key because, let's face it, consistent rent checks rely on it. When you verify their employment, you're essentially checking if their job can comfortably cover the rent.

Don't just take their word for it, though. It's a smart move to ask for some supporting documents like tax returns or bank statements. This gives you proof of the income they need so you can feel secure about their financial standing.

7. Weighs References Against On-Paper Background

Chatting with references can really help you understand who you’re dealing with. It’s one thing to see a clean record on paper; it’s another to hear firsthand about a tenant’s character and reliability. Ask previous landlords about payment habits, how the tenant treated their rental space, and if there were any notable difficulties.

Don’t forget to dig into their communication skills, too. It might seem like a small thing, but knowing if they’re prompt or if they drag their feet when responding can tell you a lot about what to expect. This can save you from potential communication headaches down the road.

8. Locates Bankruptcy Documents

Bankruptcy documents are a key piece to understanding a tenant’s financial stability. Sometimes, these details might not pop up in a regular credit check, especially if the tenant hasn’t used much credit in the past. That’s why it’s smart to look a little deeper.

Consider directing your search toward their place of work, too. It’s great if a tenant seems reliable, but what if their employer is on shaky ground? Additionally, if tenants run their own small businesses, any bankruptcy filings related to their ventures are crucial clues about the stability of their future income.

9. Alerts You of a Sexual Offense History

When screening tenants, it's crucial to be aware of any history involving sexual offenses. TruthFinder can provide detailed reports that include sex offender registry information, helping you make informed decisions about potential tenants.

10. Shows Any Involvement in Legal Battles

Uncovering a tenant’s involvement in legal issues isn’t just about finding past convictions; it also reveals if they're currently suspected of any crimes or fraud. Knowing their legal history gives you a clearer picture of what to expect and whether their past could impact their tenancy.

Moreover, knowing their legal expenses can help you assess whether they’ll be able to afford ongoing legal proceedings and timely rent payments. This insight ensures you choose tenants who are both financially stable and legally uncomplicated.

How Much Does a Background Check Cost?

The cost of a background check really depends on what you’re looking to find out. Some free background search services provide basic insights that are perfect for a quick glance at someone’s history.

Keep in mind how deep you dig can dictate the price. Extensive checks can run over $100, so consider sticking with budget-friendly options like US Search and PeopleLooker. You could even skip a few checks to save extra dollars.

How to Decide on a Screening Service

There are many factors to consider when choosing the right screening service. However, just make sure your provider complies with the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) to ensure all information is legal and accurate. This protects both your obligations and the applicant’s rights.

Here are some other factors to consider:

  • Performance history and reputation: Chat with other property managers about their experiences and recommendations. Trustworthiness comes from proven reliability.
  • Certifications and accreditations: In addition to FCRA compliance, seek out services with additional credentials, like those from the Professional Background Screeners Association (PBSA).
  • Report detail: Comprehensive tenant reports should include credit scores, criminal records, eviction histories, and rental payment records. Compare plans and pricing for the best value.
  • Service speed: When time is of the essence, choose a provider known for quick, efficient service like Instant CheckMate. This is crucial for both landlords and tenants who are in a hurry.

Empower Your Property Management with Smart Screening

Implementing a comprehensive tenant screening process is key to building a community of responsible renters and protecting your investment. By balancing thorough background checks with fair housing practices, you can create a safe living environment while minimizing risks and reducing turnover.
